{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "FULL WEBSITE BRIEF / STATIC FRONT-END ONLY

Build a complete brutalist restaurant-style website for a fictional personal blog called “The Gravel Table” — a garden-to-table outdoor dining journal by one landscape designer who hosts tiny seasonal supper nights in renovated yards. The site should feel like a restaurant site first, but the content angle is personal-blog + landscaping: essays about patios, soil, native plants, outdoor kitchens, edible borders, and the meals cooked in those spaces. IMPORTANT: this is a pure static website. No backend, no login, no database, no real reservations, no external API, no maps API, no live weather, no CMS. Use mock/static/sample content only. Everything must render locally as a static front-end.

TECH / DELIVERY
- Use React with simple UI components, CSS modules or plain CSS is fine.
- One-page long scrolling site is okay, but it must feel complex and complete with many sections.
- Static data arrays for posts, menu items, events, testimonials, garden notes, FAQs.
- No third-party service dependencies required for the page to work.
- Original design, do not copy a real restaurant or publication.
- Responsive desktop/tablet/mobile.
- Use semantic HTML where reasonable.

VISUAL STYLE
BRUTALIST RESTAURANT + LANDSCAPE BLOG
- Strong black outlines, chunky blocks, loud typography, asymmetrical cards, raw grid lines.
- Palette: bone white background, asphalt black text, mulch brown, safety orange, chlorophyll green, concrete gray.
- Texture feeling can be done with CSS patterns: diagonal hatch, dot grid, rough paper blocks, stamped labels.
- Big type headlines like menu boards, plant nursery tags, construction-site signs.
- Avoid soft corporate SaaS look. Make it editorial, bold, slightly weird, handmade.
- Simple UI only, no 3D/WebGL/canvas.

INTERACTION REQUIREMENT
- Add a confetti interaction when the user clicks the main CTA “Book A Backyard Seat” and also on “Send Me The Garden Menu”. Since this is static, it should not actually submit anywhere. Show a small inline success state like “Saved to the imaginary guest list” and trigger CSS/JS confetti pieces. No library necessary if you can make a simple DOM/CSS confetti burst.
- Also add hover states on cards/buttons: brutal offset shadow, color inversion, slight rotate.
- Sticky top nav with active-looking links is good, but no routing needed unless you want anchor links.

SITE STRUCTURE

1) TOP NAV
Logo text: THE GRAVEL TABLE
Nav links:
- Menu
- Journal
- Garden Map
- Supper Nights
- About
- FAQ
CTA button: Book A Backyard Seat
Make it sticky, chunky border, high contrast.

2) HERO SECTION
Headline: “A brutalist backyard restaurant disguised as a landscaping blog.”
Subheadline: “I redesign neglected yards, cook from the borders, and write down every muddy lesson before dinner gets cold.”
Left side: loud editorial copy and CTAs.
Right side: brutalist collage card stack, not real photos required — use CSS blocks/placeholders with labels like:
- charred leek toast
- crushed gravel patio
- basil growing through concrete
- rain barrel lemonade
Include badges:
- 12-seat fictional supper club
- 100% static website
- no reservation backend
CTA buttons:
- Book A Backyard Seat (confetti)
- Read The Latest Dirt

3) RESTAURANT MENU SECTION
Title: “This Week’s Yard Menu”
Restaurant-style menu board with categories:
SNACKS FROM THE BORDER
- Radish butter on torn rye — $8
- Fried sage gravel chips — $6
- Pickled green tomato spoon — $7
FIRE PIT PLATES
- Smoke-roasted squash with black garlic soil — $18
- Patio herb chicken with burnt lemon — $22
- Mushroom steak from the shady side yard — $21
DRINKS / NON-ALCOHOLIC
- Rain barrel mint spritz — $5
- Compost tea shrub — $6
- Cold coffee in a mason jar — $5
Make prices decorative only. Add small disclaimer: “Sample static menu, changes whenever the fictional garden does.”

4) PERSONAL BLOG / JOURNAL SECTION
Title: “Field Notes Before Service”
Create 6 article cards with date, category, title, excerpt, reading time:
- “How I Turned a Dead Parking Strip Into a Salad Bar”
- “The Patio Drainage Mistake That Ruined Soup Night”
- “Five Native Plants That Make Dinner Smell Expensive”
- “Building a Prep Table From Leftover Fence Boards”
- “Why Every Tiny Restaurant Needs a Rain Plan”
- “The Mulch Debate I Lost to a Chef”
Cards should be editorial and brutalist. Include mock tags like SOIL, SERVICE, PLANTING, FIRE, NOTES.

5) LANDSCAPING FEATURE SECTION
Title: “Yards Designed Like Dining Rooms”
Explain the core concept: landscapes are treated like restaurant rooms — arrival path, seating zones, service flow, shade, scent, sound, drainage.
Add 4 big feature blocks:
- The Entry Walk = Host Stand
- The Herb Border = Pantry
- The Fire Pit = Open Kitchen
- The Compost Corner = Dish Pit
Each block should have a bold icon-like text mark, short copy, and a mini checklist.

6) FAKE GARDEN MAP / STATIC DIAGRAM
No real map API. Make a simple static diagram with CSS boxes.
Title: “Static Garden Map, Not Google Maps”
Zones:
- Gravel Court
- Tomato Wall
- Herb Riot
- Rain Tank
- Two-Top Under Fig Tree
- Tool Shed Pantry
- Compost Throne
Add a legend and numbered labels. It should look like a folded printed map or construction blueprint but made with HTML/CSS.

7) SUPPER NIGHTS SECTION
Title: “Upcoming Fictional Supper Nights”
Create 3 event cards:
- June 21, 2026 — Solstice Weeds Dinner — 12 seats
- July 12, 2026 — Tomato Wall Tasting — 10 seats
- August 02, 2026 — Gravel & Smoke Picnic — 14 seats
Each card has menu preview, garden condition, dress code, and fake status badge like “nearly imaginary”, “mud friendly”, “static sample”.
CTA: Book A Backyard Seat with confetti. Clicking should not open a booking system.

8) ABOUT SECTION
Personal blogger voice. Name: Mara Flint (fictional). She is a landscape designer, former line cook, obsessive notebook keeper.
Write copy like:
“I started The Gravel Table after realizing every good garden already had a menu. The basil was yelling. The patio was under-seasoned. The compost pile had better structure than most dining rooms.”
Add an info card:
- Based in: Nowhere specific
- Specialty: small yards, edible borders, outdoor dining flow
- Current obsession: brutalist planters and bitter greens
- Site status: static demo / mock content

9) TESTIMONIALS / PRESS-LIKE QUOTES
Use fictional quotes only:
- “The only dinner where I left understanding drainage.”
- “Aggressively square, weirdly delicious.”
- “Our yard got better and so did the soup.”
Make them look like cut-out review slips pinned onto a board.

10) NEWSLETTER / MENU LETTER SECTION
Title: “Get The Garden Menu”
Static fake form with fields: email, favorite herb, backyard problem.
Button: Send Me The Garden Menu
On click: prevent default, show success message and confetti. No actual submission.
Include text: “Static form. Nothing is sent. The basil simply approves.”

11) FAQ SECTION
Accordion-style is okay with local state only. Questions:
- Is this a real restaurant?
- Can I actually book a seat?
- Are the blog posts real?
- Do you use a reservation system?
- Why brutalist design for gardening?
- Can this be turned into a real site later?
Answers should clearly say this is a static mock/demo and uses sample content.

12) FOOTER
Big brutal footer:
THE GRAVEL TABLE
“Dinner service for people who read seed packets.”
Links repeated, fake address: “Behind the tool shed, left of the fig tree.”
Small print: “Original static concept. No backend, no APIs, no real reservations.”

CONTENT TONE
- Witty, personal, blog-like, not generic marketing.
- Restaurant wording mixed with landscaping language.
- Make headings memorable.
- Use enough copy that the site feels alive.

DESIGN DETAILS TO INCLUDE
- Brutalist section dividers with thick borders.
- Sticker labels: NEW DIRT, SAMPLE MENU, STATIC ONLY, MUD APPROVED.
- Offset shadows on buttons/cards.
- Large numbers for sections.
- A vertical “SERVICE NOTES” sidebar on desktop if space allows.
- Mobile should stack cleanly and keep buttons usable.

IMPORTANT DO NOT ADD
- No backend/server actions.
- No database/auth/login/admin.
- No real payment or booking integration.
- No live map/weather/calendar APIs.
- No 3D, no WebGL, no game mechanics.
- No external image requirement; CSS shapes/placeholders are totally fine.

FINAL RESULT SHOULD FEEL LIKE
A complex, original, static React website for a fictional brutalist backyard restaurant that is secretly a personal landscaping blog, with mock content, editorial personality, responsive layout, and confetti CTA moments.",

  "This Week",
  "4) PERSONAL BLOG / JOURNAL SECTION Title:",
  "How I Turned a Dead Parking Strip Into a Salad Bar"
 ]

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
# webdev-structural-gate@1: necessary conditions, not a replacement judge.
_gate_layout = {}
for _line in (shot["output"] or "").splitlines():
    if _line.startswith("LAYOUT:"):
        try:
            _gate_layout = json.loads(_line[len("LAYOUT:"):])
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
        break
if (not isinstance(_gate_layout, dict) or _gate_layout.get("error")
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("text"), str)
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("scroll_w"), (int, float))
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("client_w"), (int, float))
        or _gate_layout["client_w"] <= 0):
    done(None, "Structural measurements unavailable; not scored.")
_gate_text = " ".join(_gate_layout["text"].split())
_gate_kw = cfg.get("gate_keywords") or []
_gate_fails = []
if not _gate_text:
    _gate_fails.append("blank rendered DOM")
if _gate_kw and not any(_kw.casefold() in _gate_text.casefold() for _kw in _gate_kw):
    _gate_fails.append("no brief-keyword DOM presence")
if _gate_layout["scroll_w"] > _gate_layout["client_w"] + 1:
    _gate_fails.append("horizontal overflow")
_gate_report = {"passed": not _gate_fails, "failed": _gate_fails,
                "dom_chars": len(_gate_text), "keywords": _gate_kw,
                "layout": _gate_layout}
(V / "structural_gates.json").write_text(json.dumps(_gate_report, indent=1))
if _gate_fails:
    done(0.0, "Structural gates failed: " + "; ".join(_gate_fails),
         structural_gates=_gate_fails)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Gate trivial, off-brief and overflowing pages to a scored 0 before the vision call, cutting judge spend and the blank-page lottery. Passing pages reach the judge unchanged.

gate_keywords: Saved to the imaginary guest list
How I Turned a Dead Parking Strip Into a Salad Bar
